classification_reason: The repository itself is healthy (validator 0 errors; warning baseline OK; no tracked file changed) and the tooling works after setup. But the documented setup failed with the machine's default interpreter and left a poisoned .venv that the README's own PYTHON= override could not repair, the documented quick test suite ('make test-fast') reported 34 failures in 10m51s on a healthy installation, and that test run wrote a phantom 'needs_attention' AMBIGUOUS operation (request req-bad-payload) into the learner's own operations/diagnostics store, which 'los operations' now reports as if it were the learner's.

consumer.goal: Make sure the tooling works on this machine and the repository is healthy, without changing any notes.

confusions: README says 'make setup' falls back to system python3 and 'Python 3.12+ is required' but the Makefile default PYTHON is python3 (3.11 here), so the first documented command fails.

After the failure, README's own remedy 'make setup PYTHON=python3.14' (with 3.12) still failed because the half-built 3.11 .venv was reused; nothing said to delete .venv first. The error came from pip, not from LearningOS.

'make check' reports 3 warnings but 'make warnings' says '0 warning(s) across 0 signature(s)' — they are baseline-exempt operational/clock advisories, which OPERATOR.md mentions but the output does not explain.

README describes 'make test-fast' as 'quick feedback: synthetic fixtures, no checked-in repository load'; it took 10m51s and 16 failures are FileNotFoundError on work/active/workspace-m2-exam-prep/... files that are not this learner's data, i.e. the suite does read checked-in repository content.
corrective_steps: Deleted the broken gitignored .venv created by the first failed setup and reran 'make setup PYTHON=python3.12'.
Ran 'make views' because HYGIENE-VIEWS asked for it (derived files only; allowed as an automatic permission).
consumer.outcome: Told the learner: your repository is healthy — the validator reports 0 errors, the warning baseline has no new signature, and only two advisory warnings remain (Ledgerline untouched 31 days, linear-algebra refresh untouched 104 days). No note or other tracked file was changed (git status clean before and after). Tooling works after creating a Python 3.12 environment (the machine default 3.11 is refused; I had to delete a half-built .venv). Caveat: the product's quick test suite fails 34 of ~2250 tests here, mostly because tests look for files from another person's repository, and running it left a spurious 'needs attention' operation (req-bad-payload) in your operations log that you did not cause.

friction.description: 'make setup' uses PYTHON ?= python3; on this machine that is 3.11 and pip rejects the package. The failure leaves a half-built .venv.

Retrying with the README's documented override (make setup PYTHON=python3.12) fails identically because the stale .venv keeps a 3.11 python symlink; neither the Makefile nor the error says to remove .venv.

README calls make test-fast 'quick feedback ... no checked-in repository load'; it took 10m51s and ~16 failures are FileNotFoundError on another learner's files (work/active/workspace-m2-exam-prep/outputs/...).
Running the documented test suite inside the installation writes into the learner's operational diagnostics store; nothing warns that tests share the installation root.
Validator prints '3 warning(s)' while the baseline gate prints '0 warning(s) across 0 signature(s)'; the exemption is not explained in the output.
